newsitem.title: FINLAND: LEFTISTS SHOULD QUIT "EMU GOVT" - SEPPANEN.
newsitem.headline: LEFTISTS SHOULD QUIT "EMU GOVT" - SEPPANEN.

text.p: The Leftist Party should leave government unless the government changes its policy which now aims at membership in Economic and Monetary Union in 1999, EMU critic leftist MP Esko Seppanen said on Thursday.
Seppanen won the second-most votes in the Finnish EU parliament vote on his anti-EMU views last Sunday and boosted his status in the party, by giving it two of Finland's 16 seats in the assembly.
"The government is an EMU government... it is important that (the Leftists) should not be in an EMU government and if the policy does not change, we should leave", he said.
Party leader and Culture Minister Claes Andersson said the challenge would be weighed at the party council meeting on November 30 and December 1.
Asked whether the leftists would stay in government, Andersson said: "We'll see ... The party council ... is the place to make decisions."
Seppanen said he intended to present a number of proposals at the meeting but that he was not running to become party leader, at least not yet.
"I put a lot of hopes in the party council meeting, I intend to make a number of proposals to it to resolve the situation," Seppanen told a joint news conference with the party's leaders.
Asked whether Andersson should step aside as party leader, Seppanen said "a resignation would not solve anything".
He said he may run for the post at the next party congresse in June 1998.
Andersson said the party's final stance on EMU would be determined after the economic situation in 1997 is known.
The Leftist party executive committee said in a statement that Finnish unemployment should be reduced signifcantly before Finland decides on EMU.
The whole government -- not just the leftists -- would have to revise their employment policy, Andersson said.
